title: 802.3 MAC Frame Structure
markdown:
The 802.3 MAC frame consists of these fields, left to right:

| Field | Size |
|---|---|
| Preamble | 7 bytes |
| SFD (Start Frame Delimiter) | 1 byte |
| Destination address | 6 bytes |
| Source address | 6 bytes |
| Length or type | 2 bytes |
| Data and padding | variable |
| CRC | 4 bytes |

{{viz:0}}

- **Preamble**: 56 bits of alternating 1s and 0s that alerts the
  receiving system and synchronizes its clock.
- **SFD**: the flag byte `10101011` marking the start of the frame.
- Preamble + SFD together form the **physical layer header** (not part
  of the frame itself, prepended by the physical layer).

An arrow beside the diagram indicates the frame is transmitted with
this field ordering, left field first onto the wire.

Dropping the physical-layer header (Preamble/SFD), the frame is shown
as: Destination address (6 bytes), Source address (6 bytes), Length PDU
(2 bytes), Data and padding (variable), CRC (4 bytes).

Two bracket annotations mark the payload boundaries:
- Minimum payload length: 46 bytes
- Maximum payload length: 1500 bytes

And two brackets span the whole frame:
- Minimum frame length: 512 bits (64 bytes)
- Maximum frame length: 12,144 bits (1518 bytes)

> **Note:** Frame length — Minimum: 64 bytes (512 bits). Maximum: 1518
> bytes (12,144 bits).

{{viz:1}}
